display.title: Shabbos HaGadol and Getting Ready for Pesach
display.summary_short: Why the Shabbos before Pesach is called Shabbos HaGadol, and how children can earn points in Hashem's army by helping their parents get ready for Pesach.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given the week before Pesach. Uncle Yossi asks what makes this Shabbos 'great'. On Shabbos HaGadol we begin reading the Haggadah, from Avadim Hayinu through Dayenu, where the miracles of the Exodus are told. Our Sages say that on that Shabbos, the tenth of Nissan, the Egyptian firstborn heard that the last plague was coming, rose up against their own armies and demanded that the Jews be set free, as Dovid HaMelech writes in Tehillim. Then Uncle Yossi turns to Pesach preparations as a chance for soldiers of Hashem's army to earn points: honor your parents by helping clean, put away the chametz dishes and take out the Pesach ones. He explains that the Torah forbids owning chametz on Pesach, so we burn the chametz and sell what is locked away, and children should remind their families to arrange the sale through a local rav. The clip ends there.
display.lesson: Help your parents get ready for Pesach; it is a great mitzvah of kibbud av va'em.
